# ============================================================================
# Datalog Rules for Integration Testing
# ============================================================================
# This file contains comprehensive Datalog rules for testing various aspects
# of the Datalog implementation in QLever.
#
# Syntax:
#   - Head predicate: lowercase identifier
#   - Variables: SPARQL-style (?x, ?y, ?z)
#   - IRIs: <http://example.org/resource>
#   - Comments: # or //
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 1: BASIC NON-RECURSIVE RULES
# ============================================================================

# Simple rule: parent relationship is just an alias
parent(?x, ?y) :- ?x <http://example.org/parentOf> ?y .

# Sibling rule (non-recursive)
sibling(?x, ?y) :-
  ?x <http://example.org/parentOf> ?z,
  ?y <http://example.org/parentOf> ?z,
  ?x != ?y .

# Has child (inverse of parent)
hasChild(?x, ?y) :- ?y <http://example.org/parentOf> ?x .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 2: RECURSIVE RULES - TRANSITIVE CLOSURE
# ============================================================================

# Ancestor rule - classic transitive closure example
# Base case: parent is an ancestor
ancestor(?x, ?y) :- ?x <http://example.org/parentOf> ?y .

# Recursive case: ancestor of ancestor is also ancestor
ancestor(?x, ?z) :-
  ?x <http://example.org/parentOf> ?y,
  ancestor(?y, ?z) .

# Alternative ancestor definition (different variable names)
# Base case
ancestorOf(?person, ?descendant) :-
  ?person <http://example.org/parentOf> ?descendant .

# Recursive case
ancestorOf(?person, ?descendant) :-
  ?person <http://example.org/parentOf> ?intermediate,
  ancestorOf(?intermediate, ?descendant) .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 3: GRAPH REACHABILITY
# ============================================================================

# Reachable nodes in a directed graph
# Base case: directly connected nodes are reachable
reachable(?from, ?to) :- ?from <http://example.org/edge> ?to .

# Recursive case: transitively reachable via intermediate node
reachable(?from, ?to) :-
  ?from <http://example.org/edge> ?intermediate,
  reachable(?intermediate, ?to) .

# Path length 2 (non-recursive)
pathLength2(?x, ?z) :-
  ?x <http://example.org/edge> ?y,
  ?y <http://example.org/edge> ?z .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 4: ORGANIZATIONAL HIERARCHY
# ============================================================================

# Management chain
# Base case
manages(?manager, ?employee) :-
  ?manager <http://example.org/manages> ?employee .

# Recursive case: indirect management
indirectlyManages(?boss, ?subordinate) :-
  ?boss <http://example.org/manages> ?subordinate .

indirectlyManages(?boss, ?subordinate) :-
  ?boss <http://example.org/manages> ?intermediate,
  indirectlyManages(?intermediate, ?subordinate) .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 5: FAMILY RELATIONSHIPS - COMPLEX RULES
# ============================================================================

# Grandparent (non-recursive, two levels)
grandparent(?gp, ?gc) :-
  ?gp <http://example.org/parentOf> ?p,
  ?p <http://example.org/parentOf> ?gc .

# Great-grandparent (three levels)
greatGrandparent(?ggp, ?ggc) :-
  ?ggp <http://example.org/parentOf> ?gp,
  ?gp <http://example.org/parentOf> ?p,
  ?p <http://example.org/parentOf> ?ggc .

# Cousin (children of siblings)
cousin(?x, ?y) :-
  ?px <http://example.org/parentOf> ?x,
  ?py <http://example.org/parentOf> ?y,
  ?px <http://example.org/siblingOf> ?py .

# Related (any family connection via common ancestor)
related(?x, ?y) :- ancestor(?a, ?x), ancestor(?a, ?y), ?x != ?y .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 6: RULES WITH CONSTANTS
# ============================================================================

# Descendants of Alice specifically
aliceDescendant(?x) :-
  ancestor(<http://example.org/Alice>, ?x) .

# People in the same city
sameCity(?x, ?y) :-
  ?x <http://example.org/livesIn> ?city,
  ?y <http://example.org/livesIn> ?city,
  ?x != ?y .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 7: MULTIPLE PREDICATES IN BODY
# ============================================================================

# Extended family in same location
extendedFamilyNearby(?x, ?y) :-
  ancestor(?a, ?x),
  ancestor(?a, ?y),
  ?x <http://example.org/livesIn> ?city,
  ?y <http://example.org/livesIn> ?city,
  ?x != ?y .

# Manager and friend
managerAndFriend(?m, ?e) :-
  manages(?m, ?e),
  ?m <http://example.org/friendOf> ?e .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 8: EDGE CASE RULES
# ============================================================================

# Rule with single variable (unary predicate)
isPerson(?x) :- ?x <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://example.org/Person> .

# Rule with three variables
connection(?x, ?y, ?z) :-
  ?x <http://example.org/edge> ?y,
  ?y <http://example.org/edge> ?z .

# Self-referential check
knowsSelf(?x) :- ?x <http://example.org/knows> ?x .

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 9: PERFORMANCE TEST RULES
# ============================================================================

# Deep recursion test (4+ levels)
deepAncestor(?x, ?y) :- ancestor(?x, ?y) .

# Wide recursion (multiple branches)
connected(?x, ?y) :- ?x <http://example.org/edge> ?y .
connected(?x, ?y) :- ?x <http://example.org/parentOf> ?y .
connected(?x, ?y) :- ?x <http://example.org/manages> ?y .
connected(?x, ?z) :- connected(?x, ?y), connected(?y, ?z) .

# ============================================================================
# END OF RULES
# ============================================================================
